title: Security enablement kit refresh: scope + gap analysis (FAQ + RFP library + one-pagers)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Goal: complete an inventory of the current customer-facing security FAQ + RFP/Q&A content, identify gaps vs what the field is being asked today, and turn into an actionable scope for FAQ v2 + one-pagers pack + RFP response library refresh.

Context
- This is Week 1 deliverable for the kit refresh (see PM-1847 kickoff).
- Output of this ticket feeds: (1) FAQ v2 outline + draft plan, (2) one-pager list + owners, (3) RFP library question bank mapping, (4) evidence pointer needs for internal-only index (ENG-23344).

In scope
- Inventory existing content across: prior Security FAQ, ad-hoc approved snippets used by SEs/AEs, and current RFP boilerplate.
- Identify missing topics / outdated statements / areas needing clearer Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private boundaries.
- Propose a v2 section map and ownership assignments for each gap.

Out of scope
- Implementing new controls/features (we can clarify behavior; we cannot commit to roadmap features).
- Rewriting legal templates (route to Finance/Legal via existing intake).

Sources reviewed (inventory)
1) Current Security FAQ (field PDF + older Confluence page)
- Coverage: encryption at rest/in transit (high level), basic access controls, vulnerability mgmt, incident response (inconsistent phrasing), limited Hosted vs Dedicated distinctions.
- Gaps: data residency language, retention defaults, audit log export specifics, SSO/SAML configuration details, subprocessors and DPA flow.

2) RFP boilerplate / questionnaire answers (SE shared snippets + last quarter’s response doc)
- Coverage: SOC 2 summary, general SDLC, vulnerability scanning, basic DR/BCP statements.
- Issues: inconsistent answers across reps; evidence requests handled ad-hoc; Private deployment boundary described differently in different docs.

3) Field feedback (compiled themes)
- Customers repeatedly ask for “one-pager” proof points: residency, retention, audit logs, SSO/SAML, SOC 2 scope.
- EMEA deals: residency is frequently a blocker; buyers want explicit region availability + where logs/telemetry are processed.
- Regulated prospects: want clear delineation of customer vs Redwood responsibilities in Private (VPC/on-prem).

4) Support/CS escalations (security review driven)
- Requests for written retention/deletion behavior and audit log export examples (SIEM).
- Customers ask for sample audit events and retention period for audit logs vs application logs.

Top gaps to address (must-have for v2)
A) Data residency (new content)
- Define: where customer content is processed/stored by deployment mode.
- Clarify region options for Hosted and what “residency” means (processing + storage + logs/telemetry).
- Dedicated: explain isolation + region pinning; clarify operational telemetry path.
- Private: clarify boundary (customer networking + data plane) vs Redwood control plane (if applicable).
- Deliverable: customer-facing data residency one-pager + FAQ entries.

B) Data retention & deletion controls (new content)
- Document retention defaults by data type: prompts/completions, embeddings, logs, audit logs.
- Clarify configurable retention (where available) and deletion request workflow.
- Avoid absolutes; ensure language is consistent with current product behavior and contract terms.
- Deliverable: customer-facing retention controls one-pager + FAQ entries.

C) Audit logging overview + export (expand/clarify)
- Define what’s logged today (categories) and where logs can be accessed (Console/API).
- Export: what mechanisms exist (e.g., download, API, SIEM forwarder) and what is roadmap (explicitly labeled).
- Differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Deliverable: customer-facing audit logging one-pager + FAQ entries + RFP boilerplate.

D) SSO/SAML/SCIM + RBAC details (expand)
- SSO: supported protocols (SAML), IdP compatibility (Okta/AzureAD/etc) at a high level.
- SCIM: state clearly whether supported, in pilot, or not available (no ambiguity).
- RBAC: roles and least privilege guidance; what actions are auditable.
- Deliverable: customer-facing SSO/SAML/SCIM one-pager + RBAC reference (for deep-dive) + FAQ/RFP sections.

E) Subprocessors + DPA process (new content / standardization)
- Provide a clear, repeatable answer: where to find subprocessor list, how updates are communicated, and DPA request path.
- Ensure the kit includes “how to get it” without attaching restricted artifacts broadly.
- Deliverable: one-pager section and RFP responses; link to canonical subprocessor list location.

F) SOC 2 posture (tighten)
- Standardize how we describe SOC 2 scope, report access process (under NDA), and what can be shared (e.g., bridge letters if applicable).
- Deliverable: SOC 2 one-pager + RFP boilerplate + evidence request routing.

Shared responsibility boundary (cross-cutting)
- Problem: current docs mix Hosted/Dedicated/Private responsibility statements.
- Requirement: every major topic should have a table or explicit callout: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Proposed pattern: “What Redwood manages” / “What customer manages” / “What’s configurable” per deployment mode.

Proposed deliverables mapping (outputs from this analysis)
1) Security FAQ v2
- Add sections: Residency, Retention, Audit Logging, Auth (SSO/RBAC), Subprocessors/DPA, Evidence sharing process (high-level).
- Refactor: Incident response language to be contract-dependent and avoid hard timelines.

2) One-pagers pack (customer-facing)
- Required: SOC 2 posture, Encryption + key mgmt options, SSO/SAML/SCIM + RBAC, Audit logging overview, Data residency, Data retention controls, Incident response + notification.

3) RFP response library
- Convert ad-hoc snippets into approved boilerplate with evidence pointers + “when to escalate” notes.
- Add a short “where to find it” index for AEs/SEs (Confluence canonical, Drive PDFs as attachments).

Open questions / risks (need owner confirmation)
1) Retention: confirm current defaults and what is configurable for Hosted vs Dedicated (Kevin Osei + Product).
2) Audit log export: confirm what export methods exist today and what is roadmap (Marcus Lin + Security Eng).
3) SCIM: confirm availability and exact language to use (Ethan Park + Kaitlyn Nguyen).
4) Private boundary: confirm wording for VPC/on-prem deployments (Colin O’Donnell + Vivek Kulkarni).
5) Subprocessors: confirm canonical list location and update notification mechanism (Olga Petrov + Daniel Carter).

Acceptance criteria
- A written inventory summary (this ticket) covering what exists, what’s missing, and what needs rewrite.
- A prioritized gap list with proposed deliverable(s) and owners.
- Alignment that the new topics (residency/retention/audit export/SSO/subprocessors) are included in v2 scope.

Next steps
- Create drafting tickets for each one-pager + FAQ section (tracked under PM-1847 umbrella).
- Kick off ENG-23310 for public-doc link hygiene needed by the kit.
- Ensure evidence pointers are captured in ENG-23344 (internal-only index).
comments: 2026-01-16 (Markus Klein): Field gap list matches what SEs are seeing. Biggest friction right now is (1) residency (EMEA) and (2) audit log export details for SIEM. Please make sure we explicitly call out what is available today vs planned—customers interpret vague language as commitment.

2026-01-17 (Olga Petrov): +1 on subprocessors + DPA. We need a standardized answer that points to the subprocessor list and describes the DPA request process without distributing restricted artifacts. Also please add “SOC 2 access is NDA-gated” language as a standard snippet.

2026-01-18 (Kevin Osei): For retention: we should separate (a) customer content retention (prompts/completions) from (b) operational logs/metrics and (c) audit logs. Customers often conflate these. I’ll confirm the current defaults and what’s configurable in Hosted vs Dedicated by early next week.

2026-01-20 (Marcus Lin): Audit logging: we should list event categories we can stand behind today (auth events, API key lifecycle, admin actions, model/config changes). Export mechanisms need careful wording; we have basic export workflows today but not “native SIEM push” for all modes. I’ll provide approved phrasing for the one-pager.

2026-01-22 (Naomi Feldman): Incorporated feedback and converted gaps into the must-have list above. Next action is to create one-pager drafting tasks + route the open questions to owners for confirmation so we don’t draft ourselves into a corner on retention/SCIM/audit export.
